markingPoints.description: States that the solution is very acidic
Gives the reason: 0 is the lowest value on the pH scale and it stands for a very acidic solution, since values below 7 are acidic

evidence:
The pH of a neutral solution is 7. Values less than 7 on the pH scale
represent an acidic solution.

questions.topic: Understanding the Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
questions.stem:
Meera is testing drinks in her school's science period. She dips a strip of paper into each liquid and matches the colour it turns against a printed scale of numbers running from 0 to 14. Her friend asks her how a single strip can show so many different colours, and what decides the reading Meera writes down. Meera explains that the strip is not one indicator but a mixture of several, and that each colour stands for a different concentration of hydrogen ions in the liquid. She tells her friend that a reading of 7 means the liquid is neutral, while a reading of 0 means it is very acidic.

What is the strip of paper that Meera dips into each liquid called, and what does the different colour on it tell her about the liquid? (ii) Meera finds that one liquid gives a reading of 7 and another gives a reading of 0. Which of the two is acidic, and at what reading is a liquid neutral? (iii) Meera's two friends test the same drink and get readings of 0 and 14. Whose drink has the higher hydronium ion concentration, and why?

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) Universal indicator paper; the colour shows the concentration of hydrogen ions. (ii) The liquid reading 0, since values below 7 are acidic; a liquid is neutral at 7. (iii) The friend who got 0, because the higher the hydronium ion concentration, the lower the pH value.

evidence:
We can do this by making use of a universal indicator, which is a
mixture of several indicators. The universal indicator shows different
colours at different concentrations of hydrogen ions in a solution.

The pH of a neutral solution is 7. Values less than 7 on the pH scale
represent an acidic solution.

Higher
the hydronium ion concentration, lower is the pH value.

Ravi keeps an aquarium in his room. After a spell of rainy days he finds the fish in it restless and changes the water. His science teacher tells him that rain water is not always neutral, and asks what rain water that has turned acidic should be called and what it does to the pH of a river into which it flows. She then reminds the class that the human body keeps working only within a narrow pH range, and asks the class to state that range and to say what becomes of the aquatic life in rivers into which such rain has flowed.

What should rain water that has turned acidic be called, and what does it do to the pH of the river water into which it flows? (ii) State the pH range within which the human body keeps working. (iii) Ravi notices that the fish in his aquarium become restless after the rains. Using what happens to rivers and to aquatic life when such rain flows into them, explain why.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) Acid rain; it lowers the pH of the river water. (ii) Between pH 7.0 and 7.8. (iii) Acid rain lowers the pH of the river water, and aquatic life survives only in a narrow range of pH change, so the fish find the changed pH hard to survive in.

questions.stem:
A pair of beakers stands on Priya's lab bench, one holding hydrochloric acid of one molar concentration and the other holding acetic acid of one molar concentration. Her teacher hands her a slip on which the two are named, in order, a strong acid and a weak acid, and asks her what decides which is which. Priya is also told that of two acids of equal concentration, only one gives rise to hydrogen ions in larger amount, while the other gives fewer. She asks her teacher whether the strength of an acid can be judged from its concentration alone.

On what does the strength of an acid depend? (ii) Of two acids of the same concentration, one gives rise to more hydrogen ions than the other. What is the acid that gives more hydrogen ions called, and what is the one that gives fewer called? (iii) Priya asks whether the strength of an acid can be judged from its concentration alone. Using hydrochloric acid and acetic acid of one molar concentration, answer her question.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) The strength of an acid depends on the number of hydrogen ions it produces. (ii) The one giving more hydrogen ions is a strong acid; the one giving fewer is a weak acid. (iii) No. Hydrochloric acid and acetic acid of one molar concentration produce different amounts of hydrogen ions, so strength cannot be judged from concentration alone.

evidence: The strength of acids and bases depends on the number of H ions

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
Aditi heated a few crystals of copper sulphate in a dry boiling tube. The crystals, which had looked dry all along, turned white, and she noticed droplets of water inside the tube. Her teacher asked her where that water had come from, since the crystals had never been touched with water. Aditi then added two or three drops of water to the heated sample, and the blue colour of the crystals reappeared. Her teacher asked her how many water molecules one formula unit of copper sulphate holds, and whether such crystals can really be called dry.

Water droplets appeared in Aditi's boiling tube although she had never touched the crystals with water. Where did this water come from, and what is this water called? (ii) Aditi moistened the heated sample again with water and the blue colour reappeared. Why does this show that crystals which seem dry are not really dry, and how many water molecules does one formula unit of copper sulphate hold?

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) The water came from the water of crystallisation held in the crystals; heating removed it. (ii) Crystals which seem dry hold a fixed number of water molecules in one formula unit of a salt, so moistening them brings the blue colour back and shows they were never dry. Copper sulphate has five.

evidence: crystallisation. When we heat the crystals, this water is removed and the

If you moisten the crystals again with water, you will find that blue
colour of the crystals reappears.

Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present
in one formula unit of a salt. Five water molecules are present in one
formula unit of copper sulphate.
